firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to efficiently store and retrieve hymn recordings, genres, and related metadata. It prioritizes clarity and ease of querying for the application's core features. The design uses nested collections to represent the relationships between genres, hymns, recordings, and marks. Each level of nesting reflects a one-to-many relationship, ensuring data integrity and optimized queries.

Authorization Independence:
This design doesn't require denormalization because there are no explicit authorization requirements mentioned in the prompt. All data is assumed to be publicly accessible, meaning no user-specific roles or permissions are needed.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters):
Since the data is publicly accessible and no security rules are applied, QAPs are inherently supported. List operations on any collection will return all documents without filtering based on access rights.

Invariants:
The structure supports invariants by clearly defining the parent-child relationships. For example, each hymn belongs to a genre, each recording belongs to a hymn, and each mark belongs to a recording. This ensures that all data is logically organized and easy to navigate.
